title: Bounded input rewind
statement: Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer, let $S$ be a state set, and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. Suppose a machine with $k$ work tapes has states $\mathrm{start}$ and $\mathrm{scan}$ and a destination state that may be absent. From $\mathrm{start}$, every transition moves the input head left and enters $\mathrm{scan}$, regardless of the scanned symbols; in $\mathrm{scan}$, every transition on an input bit moves left and stays in $\mathrm{scan}$, while a transition on a blank input cell moves right and enters the destination state. Then from every configuration $c$ in state $\mathrm{start}$, there is a number of steps $r \leq c$'s input-head position plus $2$ after which the state is the destination and the input-head position is $1$.
hypotheses_covered: State set $S$ and Boolean input word $x$
Transitions from start always move left and enter scan
In scan, transitions on bits move left and stay in scan
In scan, transitions on a blank move right and enter the optional destination
